## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Single-blind: the guidelines say the journal "uses a single-blind, multi-step review process" (https://web.archive.org/web/20250113213859/https://asistdl.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/23301643/homepage/forauthors). Steps: format screening, assessment of fit and quality by the editor-in-chief, assignment to a review editor, then at least two and typically three or more referees |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Not stated on the guidelines page. Authors receive copies of the referees' comments (same page) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | The guidelines say the journal seeks final decisions after no more than two major revision cycles (same page). SciRev (n=4) reports an average of 1.7 rounds (https://scirev.org/journal/journal-of-the-association-for-information-science-and-technology/). The guidelines add: there is no formal appeals process, and concerns go to the editor-in-chief |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Authors are encouraged to name up to three preferred reviewers; separately, authors must declare conflicts of interest during submission, including relationships with possible reviewers, by naming those individuals so they are not selected (same guidelines page). The editor-in-chief's editorial note adds that authors may optionally suggest board members as review editors (https://informationmatters.org/?p=27733) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes: the journal's own guidelines have a section "Uses and Roles of Generative AI" (Wayback copy 2025-01-13, https://web.archive.org/web/20250113213859/https://asistdl.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/23301643/homepage/forauthors) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate; mandatory disclosure, with one barred category of use |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 (this pass's own rubric: allowed with mandatory disclosure = 3, lowered by one because the journal bars generative AI from creating, modifying or solely analysing data) |
| **Summary** | Authors must declare all uses of generative AI in the cover letter, the methods section and other places as appropriate; authors remain responsible for accuracy, including citations. Generative AI cannot be used to create, modify or solely analyse data, cannot be a co-author and cannot act as a reviewer. The editor-in-chief has discretion in assessing authors' use. Retrieved via Wayback copy 2025-01-13 |
| **Source URL** | https://web.archive.org/web/20250113213859/https://asistdl.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/23301643/homepage/forauthors |

### Preprint Policy

> Publisher-level policy (Wiley), not journal-specific. Source: https://authorservices.wiley.com/author-resources/Journal-Authors/licensing/self-archiving.html (retrieved 2026-11-23). That page says society partners may have their own policies; the journal-specific embargo was not looked up (the publisher points to its Author Compliance Tool, which was not used). The journal's guidelines contain no preprint rule (the words preprint and self-archiving do not occur on the 2025-01-13 copy); they ask authors of accepted manuscripts to update pre-publication versions with a link to the published article.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes (publisher policy) | The submitted version may go on a personal website, an institutional repository or not-for-profit subject preprint servers, with no embargo; Wiley says authors need not remove preprints from non-profit servers before submission |
| Under review | Blank | The Wiley page speaks of the submitted version; it does not separately address the under-review stage |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes, with embargo | Wiley states 12 months for scientific, technical, medical and psychology journals and 24 months for social science and humanities journals after final publication. Embargo: not confirmed for this journal |
| Version of Record | Not allowed to replace the accepted version | The Wiley page says the accepted version cannot be updated or replaced with the Version of Record |

## Format

> Source for every row: the journal's author guidelines, Wayback copy dated 2025-01-13 (https://web.archive.org/web/20250113213859/https://asistdl.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/23301643/homepage/forauthors); the live page was not readable.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research Articles (the primary type), Brief Communications, Opinion Papers, Letters to the Editor, Book Reviews and Special Issues. Literature reviews are directed to the sister publication ARIST and review manuscripts sent to JASIST are returned |
| **Word limit** | Research Article up to 7,000 words; qualitative, field-based or ethnographic work up to 8,500 words (contact the editor-in-chief first); Brief Communication 1,000-2,000; Opinion Paper 2,000-3,000; Letter 450 words inclusive with at most three references. The count includes body, tables, captions and appendices and excludes the abstract, keywords, references and supplemental material |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Partly: revised manuscripts may be up to 10% longer, and authors are told to consult the editor-in-chief before submitting a longer manuscript. Non-compliant submissions are stated to be returned |
| **Abstract limit** | Maximum 200 words, required for all articles including Brief Communications |
| **Reference limit** | No cap stated; references are outside the word count. APA style required; manuscripts with numbered references are returned |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed and excluded from the word count. The journal provides no hosting or curation for data or code; authors are expected to keep the data set of record |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No numeric limit stated. Figures: tiff, eps, png or jpg, uploaded separately and named sequentially; tables made with the word processor's table tool |
| **Style / submission format** | APA style, with single or 1.5-line spacing preferred (not mandated); endnotes not footnotes; Word (.doc, .docx, .rtf) or LaTeX (PDF plus source files); title page with names, affiliations, full addresses and e-mail; submission through ScholarOne (https://mc.manuscriptcentral.com/jasist); cover letter encouraged; papers extending a conference paper must contain more than 30% new material and include the conference paper as a supplement; English only |

The guidelines name "empirical, contextual, conceptual, computational, political, and ontological" understandings of information as the journal's range. Most cited in the window: a 2023 article on ChatGPT and academic research papers (https://doi.org/10.1002/asi.24750, 1419 OpenAlex citations) and a 2022 article on AI and academic library work (https://doi.org/10.1002/asi.24635, 359) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, a scope condition: an ideal manuscript should "explicitly engage" information representation, information organisation, human-information interaction or the impacts of information and information technology, and authors are asked to be explicit about how these concepts are developed; submissions must be situated in the literatures the journal's readers use (author guidelines, Wayback copy 2025-01-13, https://web.archive.org/web/20250113213859/https://asistdl.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/23301643/homepage/forauthors).
- **What kind of engagement?** Engagement with information as an object of study, whatever the discipline. The guidelines say studies of single tools or techniques are welcome only if the scope extends beyond one software or narrow technique and involves studies of use, and methodological innovations must show why the method is unique and yields evidence not otherwise achievable. On the cover letter the two sources differ in strength: the guidelines copy only "encourages" one (Format), while the editor-in-chief's note says the journal requires one with every submission. The note also says that a first indicator of fit and quality is whether the manuscript follows the author guidance (https://informationmatters.org/?p=27733).
- **Article type and length**: Research Article up to 7,000 words, up to 8,500 for qualitative work after contacting the editor-in-chief; abstract up to 200 words; APA style (see Format).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: archived call "Re-orienting Search Engine Research in Information Science" (guest editors named on the society's page; submissions due 2022-11-30; https://www.asist.org/?p=84314). Two further call titles listed on the guidelines page: "The Theory and Practice of Informational Transitions" and "Healthier Information Ecosystems" (titles only).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: stated: the guidelines say submissions seen as out of scope or non-compliant are returned, and language that is not clear formal English is returned without review (Wayback copy 2025-01-13). The editorial note says desk rejections have grown faster than submissions (https://informationmatters.org/?p=27733). No percentage exists.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are records of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex: 637 records, 440 with an abstract) whose title or abstract matches the regex named in the regex table (AI-Research Notes). Shares use 440 as denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | experiments or user studies 48 (10.9%); surveys or questionnaires 29 (6.6%); "quantitative" 22 (5.0%). The guidelines list "experiments" among welcomed approaches (Wayback copy 2025-01-13) |
| Qualitative interviews | 4 | interviews 63 (14.3%); "qualitative" 37 (8.4%). Editorial statement: the guidelines carry a section "Specific encouragement for qualitative research" with a longer limit of 8,500 words (https://web.archive.org/web/20250113213859/https://asistdl.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/23301643/homepage/forauthors) |
| Autoethnography | 2 | Ethnography or autoethnography terms 6 (1.4%) (the regex does not separate the two). The guidelines name "ethnographic approaches" among welcomed approaches (same page) |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | theory or conceptual wording 126 (28.6%); the regex is broad, since "theory" also appears in applied papers. The guidelines require research articles to be "grounded in theory" (same page) |
| Mixed methods | 1 | "mixed methods" 3 (0.7%) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 2 | systematic, scoping or meta-analytic review wording 12 (2.7%). The guidelines send literature reviews to the sister publication ARIST and return review manuscripts to the sender (same page) |
| Bibliometric / scientometric (added row) | 3 | 32 (7.3%); OpenAlex's top topic for the journal is scientometrics (575 topic assignments, see Subject Density) |
| Machine learning / language-model methods (added row) | 3 | 45 (10.2%) |
| Case study (added row) | 3 | 30 (6.8%) |
| Content analysis, thematic analysis or grounded theory (added row) | 3 | 29 (6.6%) |

The words ethical approval, ethics committee, informed consent and institutional review do not occur in the guidelines copy of 2025-01-13 (searched, 0 hits); the page points to Wiley's publishing-ethics guidance and COPE (https://web.archive.org/web/20250113213859/https://asistdl.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/23301643/homepage/forauthors). Authors must declare conflicts of interest and disclose funders |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers appear: 71 of 416 articles in the window (OpenAlex, retrieved 2026-11-23); three-or-more-author papers are 250 of 416 |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | No independent-scholar rule stated. The title page must give each author's affiliation and full address (Wayback copy 2025-01-13). The board copy lists two editorial-board entries whose affiliation is a consultancy or company rather than a university (Connecting Stones Consulting; SciTech Strategies, Inc.; https://web.archive.org/web/20250811064435/https://asistdl.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/23301643/homepage/editorialboard); that says nothing about acceptance odds |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Authors are expected to keep the data set or code used (the "data set of record") in case concerns arise, following COPE; the journal provides no hosting or curation; no deposit mandate is stated (Wayback copy 2025-01-13). Data citation in the reference list is requested |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Single-blind review means authors are known to referees and names go on the title page (Wayback copy 2025-01-13). Pre-submission preprints are allowed by the publisher (https://authorservices.wiley.com/author-resources/Journal-Authors/licensing/self-archiving.html), so no anonymity is expected |
| **AI use** | Declare all generative AI use in the cover letter and methods; generative AI cannot create, modify or solely analyse data and cannot be an author or reviewer (Wayback copy 2025-01-13) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; APC listed by OpenAlex at USD 3310; 218 of 416 recent articles are hybrid OA (see Open Access) |
| **Conflicts and funding** | Authors must name possible reviewers with whom they have relationships so that they are not chosen, and disclose funding names and sources (Wayback copy 2025-01-13) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope and compliance**: the guidelines say submissions seen as out of scope or non-compliant are returned, including papers without APA style (numbered references, numbered headings or two-column layout are named), and manuscripts that are mainly a literature review (Framing Requirements, Format; Wayback copy 2025-01-13).
- **Length**: a research article is capped at 7,000 words, or 8,500 for qualitative work after contacting the editor-in-chief; revisions may exceed it by up to 10% (Format).
- **Generative AI**: undeclared use breaches the journal's own rule, and using generative AI to create, modify or solely analyse data is barred (AI Policy).
- No ethics-approval or data-deposit requirement is stated on the archived page, so none is listed as a blocker (Practical Concerns).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: SciRev (n=4) reports about 2.5 months for a first review round and 5.6 months total for accepted manuscripts (Review Cycle Time); the sample is too small to treat as typical, and no publisher figure was readable.
- **Open access cost**: gold OA carries an APC, listed by OpenAlex at USD 3310 (Open Access); green deposit of the accepted version is subject to the publisher's embargo of 12 or 24 months depending on subject classification, not confirmed for this journal (Preprint Policy).
- **Cover letter, formatting and editing**: the guidelines copy encourages a cover letter, while the editor-in-chief's note says one is required (https://informationmatters.org/?p=27733; Framing Requirements); the guidelines say manuscripts not in APA style are returned for correction (Format); the note says poorly written manuscripts struggle in peer review and suggests a professional editor (Voice & Style).
- **Editorial transition**: the editor-in-chief named on the society page differs from the 2025-08-11 board copy, so current practice may differ from the archived guidelines (Identity).

### Best Suited For

- Studies of information use, retrieval, organisation or scholarly communication with a stated link to information science literature: top topics are scientometrics and information retrieval, and information behaviour appears in 14.8% of recent abstracts (Subject Density, Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Qualitative and field-based work needing up to 8,500 words: the journal states this encouragement (Format, Methodological Preferences).
- Computational and bibliometric studies with evidence of use: 10.2% and 7.3% of recent abstracts, and the guidelines accept computational work if the scope extends beyond one tool (Methodological Preferences, Framing Requirements).
- Authors from outside information science who bring an information focus: the guidelines name communication, HCI, STS, information systems and computing (Orientation).

### Not Recommended For

- Literature reviews as the main contribution: the guidelines return such manuscripts and send them to the sister publication ARIST (Format).
- Studies of a single software tool with no study of use: the guidelines welcome tool studies only if the scope extends beyond one software or narrowly defined technique and includes studies of use (Framing Requirements).
- Authors who need an acceptance rate or turnaround before choosing: neither was readable; SciRev has four reviews (Metrics, Review Cycle Time).
- Authors needing double-blind review: the journal states single-blind (Peer Review).
